Tidal mill

A tidal mill is a mill powered by the rise and fall of the tide. Unlike a watermill on a river, it depends on a storage pond that fills at high water and empties through the mill race at low water.

History

Tidal mills are recorded along the Atlantic coast from the early medieval period. Most were used for grinding grain and remained in service until steam power displaced them.

Mechanism

The pond is closed by a sluice at high tide. When the tide falls, the difference in level drives water through the wheel.

  • Pond: stores water at high tide
  • Sluice: controls the intake and protects the wheel
  • Race: carries water to the wheel

Surviving examples

Roughly forty structures survive in some form, of which fewer than ten retain their machinery.
